subject: Keystone POC — success signals, ops owners, and next steps
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Verma <aisha@keystoneai.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-27T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Keystone POC — success signals, ops owners, and next steps

Hi Aisha — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposal for the proof-of-concept acceptance criteria + who's owning what. I tried to keep this tight so we can confirm and get the kickoff on calendar.

Summary (high level)
- Goal: Validate Keystone's low-latency answer generation for customer-facing workflows and measure production unit economics under a representative synthetic workload.
- Duration: 3 weeks of active testing (canary + scaled run), followed by a 1-week readout. Target kickoff: week of 2026-10-11.

Proposed success signals (please confirm):
1) Latency: P95 generation latency for 512-token prompts <= 300 ms (target) / <= 400 ms (pass). For high-priority payment flows, aim for P95 <= 250 ms (Aisha, you flagged this).
2) Throughput: Sustained 25 requests/sec per model instance with tail-latency targets maintained.
3) Cost: Observed token cost <= $0.005/token at scale (measured as tokens billed / tokens generated across test window).
4) Quality: Human-eval pass rate >= 88% on the customer-defined rubric for the 200-sample evaluation set (we'll collaborate on rubric).
5) Reliability: No more than 1 partial-failure event per 48 hours (partial = degraded quality or fallback to smaller model), and automatic fallback works end-to-end.

Operational owners (Redwood / Keystone):
- Redwood runtime setup & model pinning: Diego Fernandez (me) — infra + canary config.
- Eval rubric & sample set: Aisha Verma (Keystone) + Monica Patel (Redwood) to co-own labeling pass.
- Observability & cost telemetry: Ben Carter (Redwood).
- Security/compliance checklist: Keystone to share the SOC2 / legal requirements; Redwood will provide KMS/HSM options during private deployment if needed.

Next steps (actionable)
- Aisha: share the 200-sample rubric + any high-priority payment prompts by 2026-10-04.
- Diego: deliver POC runbook + calendar invite for kickoff by 2026-10-06 (attached draft runbook).
- Ben: prepare telemetry dashboard template and approximate cost projection for the 3-week run by 2026-10-07.

Attachment: keystone-poc-success-slate.xlsx (success signals and owner table - draft)

If that looks OK I will lock the kickoff and schedule a 30-minute kickoff for the week of 10/11.

Thanks — Diego
Diego Fernandez
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Redwood Inference — developer-first inference (redwood.com)
From: Aisha Verma <aisha@keystoneai.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Lee <tom@keystoneai.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-28T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Keystone POC — success signals, ops owners, and next steps

Diego — thanks for the thoughtful recap and the attachment. Quick notes from our side: we broadly agree, a few tweaks below.

- Latency: for the payment flow we need P95 <= 250 ms. For other flows 300 ms target / 400 ms pass is fine.
- Throughput: 25 req/s per instance is reasonable; we will also want a short 30-min soak at 2x load to check degradation modes.
- Cost: we expect your number to be close; please include scenario with prefix caching enabled (saves ~20% tokens on our side).
- Quality: we'll push over a 200-sample set from our Product team by 2026-10-04 (Tom will own).
- Security: can you attach your standard SOC2 evidence packet or a pointer to the compliance page? We will need that for procurement.

Timeline: kickoff week of 10/11 works for us. We may require a short legal NDA addendum; I'll flag to procurement and share any redlines by 2026-10-06.

Thanks — looking forward.
Aisha
Aisha Verma
Head of Product, Keystone AI

- Define human-eval criteria and gold labels for the 200 samples.

Ben:

I'll take point on scheduling: I will propose kickoff slots for 10/11–10/15 and include a short agenda (goals, success metrics review, ops runbook, timeline).

Thanks — Diego
